task_instance: Run one minimal cli-exercise case: launch a trivial CLI subject (e.g. a script that prints a prompt and reads one line of input) through the skill's described flow -- start an isolated run via 'the Go helper's run command' with a preflight receipt and approved contract, observe terminal state via the Tuistory client, send one exercise action, capture validation, and finish with exit-status/timestamp metadata in a session manifest.
blocker_detail: The skill is an internal (user-invocable: false) orchestration layer that mandates a specific proprietary toolchain: a compiled 'Go helper' binary exposing a 'run' command that owns the subject process, checks an executable checksum, and enforces 'contract'/'preflight receipt' schemas; a Node-based 'Tuistory' adapter that supplies a terminal client for reading actual terminal state and sending revision-checked actions; and companion reference documents (../../references/runtime-interface.md, controllers.md, recording-sessions.md) plus a sibling cli-exercise-evidence skill for reporting. None of this exists in the environment or repo: `grep -ril tuistory /home/user/skill-achievability-compiler` only finds other SKILL.md prompt/benchmark files that mention the name, never an implementation; there is no runtime-interface.md/controllers.md/recording-sessions.md anywhere under ce_sources; only a Go toolchain (/usr/local/go/bin/go) is present with no corresponding source to build the described helper. Building a compliant replacement from scratch (its own contract/receipt schema, checksum verification, terminal-observation client, controller interpreter, manifest/evidence conventions) would not be 'accomplishing the skill' but inventing a different, unspecified system -- the skill's core deliverable (a receipted, checksum-verified, controller-driven recording session with a specific Go+Tuistory runtime) depends on tooling this runtime does not provide and cannot be substituted for while still exercising what the skill actually describes.
evidence: Read /home/user/skill-achievability-compiler/benchmark/ce_sources/cli__cli__cli-exercise-run/SKILL.md in full. Confirmed absence of referenced infra: `find ... -iname runtime-interface.md -o -iname controllers.md -o -iname recording-sessions.md` returned nothing. `ls .../cli__cli__cli-exercise-run/` shows only SKILL.md and LICENSE, no references/ dir, no code. `grep -ril tuistory /home/user/skill-achievability-compiler` matched only other SKILL.md files and benchmark run-log JSON prompts (data about the skill, not an implementation) -- no source code, binary, or package for a 'Tuistory' client or a Go 'run' helper exists anywhere in the environment. `which go` shows a Go toolchain is installed but there is no source to build the described helper from. Concluded the task cannot be attempted as specified without inventing the entire proprietary runtime the skill assumes.
